evidence: event_append.py:239 `lambda: _with_transient_head_retry(` inside `_git_commit`, event_append.py:277 inside `_git_commit_paths`, event_append.py:633 in the UU-recovery commit — all wrap `subprocess.run` resolved as `event_append.subprocess.run`
test_txn_transient_retry.py:60 `monkeypatch.setattr(gitutil.subprocess, "run", fake_run)` — the injection point is gitutil, not event_append
search of tests for `_with_transient_head_retry` returns no matches; search for `could not parse` in tests hits only test_txn_transient_retry.py (transition path)
Commit message claims: 'Also wrap event_append's `_git_commit`, `_git_commit_paths` and the UU-recovery commit … so every store-path `git commit` self-heals' — this claimed behavior is untested
advisory.finding: event_append's three HEAD-retry-wrapped commit sites (`_git_commit`, `_git_commit_paths`, and the UU-recovery commit) have zero test coverage for the transient `could not parse HEAD` self-heal. The only new test drives the transition path through gitutil's `run_git_write` (it monkeypatches `gitutil.subprocess.run`), which cannot exercise event_append's commits — those call `_with_transient_head_retry` directly over `event_append.subprocess.run`, a distinct dispatch seam.
scenarios: A future refactor removes/reverts the `_with_transient_head_retry` wrapper on `_git_commit_paths` or the UU-recovery commit; the suite stays green while a delete/event-append commit again loses a write to the runner-FS HEAD blip

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that keeps returning the transient `could not parse HEAD` signature on every commit attempt and asserts the operation surfaces a failure after `_TRANSIENT_HEAD_ATTEMPTS` (and does not loop indefinitely).
evidence: gitutil.py:213-220 `for attempt in range(1, _TRANSIENT_HEAD_ATTEMPTS): … result = run_once(); return result` — terminal branch has no coverage
test_txn_transient_retry.py:56-57 fails only `state["commits"] == 1`, so attempt 2 succeeds via real_run; the non-transient test at :92 never matches the marker
ABSENCE: no test asserts behavior after the attempt cap is exhausted with a persistently-transient signature
advisory.finding: The exhaustion path of `_with_transient_head_retry` (all `_TRANSIENT_HEAD_ATTEMPTS` attempts fail with the transient signature) is untested. Both tests inject the fault on only the first attempt (self-heal) or use a non-transient signature (immediate surface); nothing asserts the loop terminates and returns the final failing result after the attempt cap when the transient never clears.
scenarios: A persistent (not self-healing) HEAD-parse fault: the retry must eventually surface the failure rather than loop or swallow it; an off-by-one in the loop bound would go undetected

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a direct `_is_transient_head_error` classifier test covering case-insensitivity and the stdout fallback (mirroring the add-side `_is_transient_add_error` tests).
evidence: gitutil.py:198 `low = text.lower()` (case-insensitive) and gitutil.py:216 `_is_transient_head_error(result.stderr or result.stdout or "")` (stdout fallback) — neither exercised
test_event_append_transient_retry.py:47-60 shows the established pattern of direct `_is_transient_add_error` classifier tests, absent here for `_is_transient_head_error`
test_txn_transient_retry.py:32 `_COULD_NOT_PARSE_HEAD = "fatal: could not parse HEAD"` injected only via stderr with fixed casing
advisory.finding: The `_is_transient_head_error` classifier's documented case-insensitive matching and its stdout fallback (`result.stderr or result.stdout`) are not directly pinned, unlike the add-side sibling which has dedicated classifier tests. The injected fixture always supplies a lowercase-matchable stderr, so a regression narrowing the marker or dropping the stdout fallback would not be caught.
scenarios: git emits the signature on stdout, or with different casing; a tightened marker set silently stops matching
